text:
Elena: Heads-up — vendor VeloData Sp. z o.o. (PL) invoiced Redwood GmbH (DE) and is asking us to "gross-up" for a 12% Polish withholding. They didn't charge VAT on the PDF. Anyone seen this before? :thinking:

Mark: Do not gross-up without docs. Which Redwood legal entity is on the invoice? That decides reverse-charge vs withholding.

Elena: Invoice shows Payee: Redwood GmbH, Germany. Invoice snippet copied from Coupa: ```
Invoice#: 2026-05-02-VD-987
Supplier: VeloData Sp. z o.o.
Tax ID: PL5223341158
Amount: EUR 6,750
Description: Data pipeline implementation (remote)
Vendor note: "Please gross-up 12% to cover Polish withholding tax so supplier receives net after WHT."
```

Tomasz: Quick tax view (Poland): Poland can impose withholding on certain cross-border payments (e.g., royalties, some technical services), but EU rules and place-of-supply for B2B services matter. Since invoice is to a German entity, German reverse charge for services might apply — then the supplier shouldn't be demanding Polish WHT.

Tomasz: Also, domestic Polish WHT generally relates to payments made by Polish payers or where Polish law specifically taxes the service. A Polish supplier invoicing a DE company claiming PL WHT is unusual. Ask for the legal basis.

AP: I've placed the invoice on HOLD in the system. Please provide exact wording we should request from vendor so we can forward.

TaxTeam: Request from vendor: (1) formal citation of the Polish tax law or authority decision they rely on; (2) a Polish tax assessment/notice if they claim WHT was applied; (3) a Polish certificate of tax residency and any treaty article they rely on (Poland–Germany treaty). If they expect us to withhold, they must give instructions and documentation for the remittance and credit claim.

Elena: Draft vendor reply I'll send: "We cannot gross-up without documentation. Please provide the legal basis for the 12% Polish withholding (statute or tax authority notice), a tax residency certificate, and a revised invoice that clarifies VAT/tax treatment and the invoiced legal entity. Payment will remain on hold until we receive and validate these documents." Thoughts?

Mark: Sounds right. If they insist it's a contractual commercial term, they must attach the contract clause. Otherwise decline gross-up and suggest they reissue with VAT/reverse-charge wording or seek local counsel.

Tomasz: If vendor later provides a Polish assessment showing WHT applies despite a German payer, we should escalate to Legal to review risk and contract obligations. But operationally we don't gross-up automatically.

AP: HOLD flag set for invoice 2026-05-02-VD-987 by AP — reason: awaiting vendor tax docs.

invoice-bot: Payment status updated: ON HOLD for invoice 2026-05-02-VD-987 (VeloData Sp. z o.o.) — awaiting tax documentation.
